clue.text: Took a trip in China, maybe, and was ruined

definitions.text: Took a trip in China, maybe
definitions.meaning: a tourist visiting the Great Wall of China literally travelled to that famous barrier
an idiom for a business failing or going bankrupt

explanation.surface: A traveller's holiday in China went badly and left them broke.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is literal and playful: a visit to the Great Wall. The second is the idiom for collapsing financially.
explanation.definitionFit: Going under financially is what the idiom describes, the image being of someone pushed back against a barrier with no escape.

clue.text: Perform duty as cleric and celebrate new life

definitions.meaning: a priest at a christening pours water on the infant's crown
a British idiom for having a drink to mark a birth

explanation.surface: A vicar does his job and the family marks a baby's arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the phrase is everyday slang for toasting a newborn with drinks, usually by the father and friends; here it is also read literally as baptism.
explanation.definitionFit: Baptism involves sprinkling an infant, and the same phrase is British slang for a celebratory drinking session after a birth.

clue.text: Conan Doyle's hero finally changing sides in this country

indicators.note: the last letter swaps from one side to the other, left becoming right

parts.note: Sir Nigel Loring is the knightly hero of Conan Doyle's novels Sir Nigel and The White Company

explanation.surface: A fictional hero switches allegiance at the end of his adventures abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Holmes is the obvious first thought but leads nowhere. 'Sides' are L (left) and R (right): the final L of the hero's name is swapped for R.
explanation.definitionFit: A West African state, landlocked and named after the great river that flows through it.

clue.text: Change exercises with no one joining class

indicators.note: the following piece is taken away from the word before it

parts.note: to exercise is to train, so 'exercises' as a verb gives this word
one is I, the Roman numeral
a form is a class or year group in a British school

explanation.surface: A fitness routine is altered so that nobody turns up to the class.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter something completely in form or nature is to convert it, a synonym of change.

clue.text: Big wave has girl engulfed in flying mist

indicators.note: the girl is swallowed up inside the letters of the other piece
flying suggests the letters of mist scattering through the air into a new order

parts.note: Una is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A huge wave sweeps over a girl lost in drifting fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' makes TSMI from the fog word, and 'engulfed in' sets the girl's name in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidal surge caused by an undersea earthquake is a very large ocean swell.

clue.text: Praise bringing old flame reverse of fortune

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: the word that follows is read backwards

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate or fortune

explanation.surface: Someone thanks a former lover who brought a change of luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse of' turns LOT into TOL.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud or glorify someone is to speak highly of them.

clue.text: Macedonian general not supporting governor

parts.note: being anti something is opposing it
governor is old British slang for one's father, as is the Latin word pater

explanation.surface: An ancient soldier refuses to back the provincial ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Governor' (or 'guv'nor') is old British slang for father.
explanation.definitionFit: He served Philip II and Alexander the Great, ruling Macedon as regent while Alexander campaigned in Asia.

clue.text: A mere illusion?

parts.note: a mere is a lake, so this is a lake's imaginary creature, the famous Scottish beast many believe never existed

explanation.surface: Something dismissed as merely imaginary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mere' looks like 'only', but it is the noun for a lake, and a loch is a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary creature of a Highland lake is widely held to be a fantasy, so a lake's illusion.

clue.text: Son with name for being "one of the boys"

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies
a tag is a label or name

explanation.surface: A son is called something that marks him as a regular lad.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is in quotes: a stag party or stag night is men only.
explanation.definitionFit: Stag describes an all-male gathering, so a man attending one is one of the lads.

clue.text: A film formerly was deemed suitable for one

definitions.text: A film formerly was deemed suitable for one

parts.words: A film formerly was deemed suitable for one
parts.note: the old British A certificate marked a film as meant for grown-ups rather than children

explanation.surface: A movie was once judged fit for a particular viewer.
explanation.walkthrough: Britain's former film classification used 'A' for films more suitable for grown-up audiences; 'A film' is that certificate, not just any film.
explanation.definitionFit: A grown-up was the intended audience for such a rated film.

clue.text: Arachnid in bed cover

definitions.meaning: a small blood-sucking parasite related to spiders and mites
the strong fabric case of a mattress or pillow

explanation.surface: A small creature lurks in the bedding.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the old word for a mattress case, from which 'ticking' fabric gets its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an eight-legged parasite and the cloth casing that holds a mattress's stuffing.

clue.text: A march is organised for big appeal

indicators.note: the words are put into a new order, as a march is organised into ranks

explanation.surface: A protest march is arranged because it has wide public support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges A MARCH IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Charm or magnetism that draws people to someone is a strong personal attraction.

clue.text: Like phoney grandma given flower before end of tale

parts.note: a lupin is a garden flower with tall spikes

indicators.note: the last letter of the word that follows is taken

explanation.surface: A fake grandmother is handed a bloom just before the story ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The phoney grandma is the wolf disguised as Red Riding Hood's grandmother, so 'like' her means wolfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfish is the meaning, and the fake grandmother of the fairy tale was a wolf.

clue.text: A loss of bodily fluid restricting person, one built like a sailor?

indicators.note: the outer piece hems in the inner ones, holding them inside

parts.note: a bleed is a loss of blood
bod is British slang for a person
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone loses blood while sturdily built like a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricting' sets the person and the one inside the blood loss. The definition plays on able seaman, a sailor's rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Fit and strong in body, with a nod to the naval rank of able seaman.

clue.text: Leaves without the others to cancel order at newsagent?

definitions.meaning: the blank sheets at the front and back of a book, outside the printed pages
read as stop the delivery of newspapers, a whimsical second meaning

explanation.surface: Someone goes off without the rest to stop the paper delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb but means pages. In Britain, newsagents deliver newspapers on order; ending that order is cutting off the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the blank sheets pasted inside a book's covers, outside all the other pages.

clue.text: See dry rot that's ruined ship

indicators.note: the words, wrecked like rotten timber, are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ship's woodwork has been destroyed by fungal decay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's ruined' rearranges SEE DRY ROT.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast warship is a type of naval vessel.

clue.text: Examine sort of shell

definitions.meaning: to try out or check something
the hard outer casing of a sea urchin or similar creature

explanation.surface: Someone inspects a kind of seashell.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a zoologist's word for the hard case of creatures like sea urchins.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to try something out and the shell-like covering of certain marine invertebrates.

clue.text: Be taken in by commercial that's lying

indicators.note: the first piece is enclosed by the advert word

parts.note: an ad is a commercial or advertisement

explanation.surface: Someone is fooled by a dishonest advertisement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lying' means reclining, not telling untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: In bed is lying down, an old-fashioned word for being in bed.

clue.text: Most realms after revolution become disorderly states

indicators.note: an uprising turns the kingdoms upside down, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Most kingdoms fall into chaos after an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after revolution' rearranges the two opening words; 'become' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Whirlpools, and figuratively scenes of confused turmoil, are chaotic situations.

clue.text: Able to extend terminal, one located in city area

indicators.note: the following pieces are placed inside the postcode letters

parts.note: EC is a London postcode district covering the City
terminal means final, last
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A stretchy part of a bus terminal is found downtown.
explanation.walkthrough: EC (East Central) is the postal district of the City of London. 'Terminal' is an adjective meaning final.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stretchy can lengthen and spring back.

clue.text: Scored very classical half-century to go on the attack

parts.note: assai is the Italian musical direction for very, as written in a score
L is fifty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A batsman reaching fifty in grand style turns aggressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scored' means written in a musical score, not runs in cricket; a half-century is fifty runs.
explanation.definitionFit: To assault or attack violently is to launch an offensive.

clue.text: Caterpillar, perhaps, found in particular valley

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across these two words

explanation.surface: A caterpillar turns up in a certain valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterpillar is an example of an insect's immature form.

clue.text: I am interrupting a friend, producing resentment

indicators.note: the contraction butts into the middle of the friend phrase

parts.note: a crony is a close friend
I am contracts to I'm

explanation.surface: Cutting in on a companion causes bad feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupting' sets the contraction of the opening words inside the friend phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitterness and ill feeling between people is a synonym of resentment.

clue.text: Bike showed little sign of getting going

definitions.text: showed little sign of getting going
definitions.meaning: to have ... is to have wandered about listlessly, sulking

explanation.surface: A bike stubbornly refused to start.
explanation.walkthrough: The bike is a noun; the second sense is the past tense of a verb, unrelated in sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a small motorbike and the past tense of a verb for listless sulking.

clue.text: What sounds like top competitor at Cruft's?

parts.note: a peak is a top or summit

explanation.surface: Which dog sounds like the best one at a dog show?
explanation.walkthrough: Crufts is Britain's leading dog show; the competitor is a Pekingese.
explanation.definitionFit: A short name for a Pekingese, a toy dog breed shown at dog shows.

clue.text: Like unkempt hair man keeps dry

indicators.note: the name holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: Ray is a man's name
TT means teetotal, so not drinking: dry

explanation.surface: A man's scruffy hair stays dry.
explanation.walkthrough: TT, for teetotal, is crossword shorthand for abstaining from alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Straggly, matted hair is described as rat-like.

clue.text: Head chef's preparation

definitions.meaning: the crown of the head, especially a bald one
a savoury paste of meat or fish made by a cook

explanation.surface: A head cook prepares a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses share spelling only in unaccented form: the food word properly carries accents.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the top of the skull and a rich spread such as liver paste.

clue.text: Chaser did trip all over the place — man with a message?

indicators.note: scattered in every direction, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pursuer stumbles wildly, then turns out to be a courier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' rearranges CHASER DID TRIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorcycle courier carries messages and documents.
